headline: Red Sox Winning Streak Snapped As Bats Go Cold In Washington Loss
morning_brew: Tuesday night at Fenway Park was a complete 180 from what we saw all last week. After riding a wave of momentum, the offense just evaporated against the Nationals. Cade Cavalli was carving us up like a Thanksgiving turkey, and watching our guys manage only four hits all night was an absolute disastah. The energy that had been building around the yard felt totally deflated by the middle innings, and it left me wondering if that recent success was just a brief flash in the pan.

Early on the mound gave us four quality innings, but the bullpen had a really rough time keeping things within reach once they took over. Weissert caught the loss after things started slipping away in the later frames, and the whole night felt like a classic case of the wheels coming off right when you least expect it. My mother watched a few innings before turning it off, and she just shook her head and said they looked like they were swinging underwater. She has a way of cutting right through the noise.

Now we have to regroup and try to salvage the series here at home before hitting the road again. There is plenty of chatter around the league about the upcoming free agency period, but for us, the focus has to be on finding some consistency in the box score every single night. We aren't in a position to take any opponent lightly, especially when the bats go quiet like they did against Washington. Let's hope they wake up for the afternoon matchup.

news_digest.headline: Cade Cavalli strikes out 13 in Nationals' rout of Red Sox
news_digest.dans_take: Absolutely brutal performance from our hitters, we could not touch him all night.
